newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Short-dated dlr/yen vols well bid pre-G7.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Short-dated dlr/yen vols well bid pre-G7.

text.p: Shorter-dated dollar/yen options were well-bid in U.S. trading, despite a virtually static spot dollar, as the market began focusing on Sunday's meeting of Group of Seven (G7) rich countries, dealers said.

They said low-delta yen calls were particularly in demand because of expectation that G7 would voice concerns over the dollar's rapid ascent against the yen this year, given the resurgence of Japan's trade surplus with the United States.
"The most widely anticipated scenario is that the G7 will try to put a brake on dollar/yen," said Masao Okada, chief options dealer at Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank in New York.

"Volatilities have been under pressure for a while but they are starting to reflect that event risk," he said, adding that bids began to pick up in Thursday's European hours after staying subdued for most of Wednesday and early Thursday.
Traders said at-the-money one-week volatility was quoted at around 9.0/9.5 percent, while a 125-yen yen call -- with delta of about 35 -- was priced at 10.0/10.7 percent.

The levels compare with one- and three-month volatilities of 8.8/9.0 and 9.0/9.2 percent respectively, up 0.3 point each from Wednesday. The curve gets more steeply positive from six-month and out, with one-year at 9.7/9.9 percent.
"Everything we did today seemed to be short dates, low-delta yen calls," said an interbank broker in New York.

He said there was strong interest to buy yen calls through one-month 20-delta risk reversals -- buying yen calls with strike prices around 115 yen and selling equally low delta yen puts -- which were priced at 0.1/0.3 point favoring yen calls.
"I think a lot of people didn't have those strikes," the broker said.
Okada added that Japanese exporter firms were buying yen calls through risk reversals to lock in their dollar exposures ahead of their Golden Week holidays next week.

Traders said risk reversals were skewed toward yen calls out to the three-month area and trading near par further out the curve, reflecting the market's conviction that the dollar would head higher in the long term.
In fact, the dollar could spike up if the G7 did not express support for the yen with stronger words than it used in irs February communique, they said.

A hedge fund trader said the market next week could be driven by U.S. economic data including the April jobs report due May 2, which might pave the way for another interest rate hike at the May 20 Federal Open Market Committee meeting.

Another near-term factor much talked about was expiration on May 1 of a huge knockout option with a barrier price of around 127.30 yen. Until today's bounce, short-dated volatilities had been pressured by selling linked to gamma supplied to the interbank market by the exotic option deal.
The dollar/mark market was very quiet today, with the curve staying flat. One-month to six-month volatilities were all hovering around 8.9/9.1 percent.
Sterling volatilities were firm ahead of U.K. general elections next week. One-month cable stood at 7.3/7.6 percent, up a quarter point from late Wednesday levels.
